config.title: HOC withAuth

intro.title: HOC withAuth
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a Higher-Order Component (HOC) called `withAuth` that wraps another Vue component to add authentication logic. You will learn how to create a function that takes a component as input and returns a new, enhanced component that checks if a user is logged in before rendering. The main technologies involved are Vue's composition API, component props, and conditional rendering. This is a beginner-friendly introduction to code reuse and component composition in Vue.
intro.usecase: Higher-Order Components like withAuth are essential in real-world applications where access control is required. You'll see this pattern in admin dashboards that restrict certain features to authenticated users, e-commerce checkout flows that require login, or banking apps that protect sensitive financial data. For example, a user management panel might use withAuth to ensure only administrators can view or edit user permissions. This pattern allows developers to consistently protect routes, components, and features across complex applications while keeping authentication logic separate and reusable.

objectives: Construct a higher-order component (HOC) that wraps a Vue component to add authentication logic.
Initialize and manage authentication state within the HOC using Vue's reactivity system.
Implement conditional rendering in the HOC to display the wrapped component only when authenticated.
Apply the HOC to a target component by wrapping it with the authentication logic.
Configure the HOC to redirect unauthenticated users to a login route.
Integrate the HOC with a mock authentication service to simulate login and logout behavior.
Manipulate the authentication state to demonstrate dynamic updates in the UI.

steps.title: Import Vue and defineComponent
steps.instruction: Import Vue and defineComponent from 'vue' to set up the Vue environment for component creation.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the necessary Vue APIs from the 'vue' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing core Vue APIs
import { defineComponent } from 'vue';
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue and defineComponent APIs are imported and available for use.
successCriteria: Vue and defineComponent are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both Vue and defineComponent from the 'vue' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are not correct. You need to import Vue and defineComponent from 'vue'.

steps.title: Create the withAuth higher-order component function
steps.instruction: Create a function named withAuth that takes a component as an argument and returns a new component. The function should accept a single parameter (the component to wrap) and return a new component.
steps.hint: Think of withAuth as a function that receives a Vue component and returns another Vue component. You can start with: function withAuth(WrappedComponent) { return defineComponent({ ... }); }

steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a withAuth function that takes a component parameter and returns a new component created with defineComponent.
successCriteria: The withAuth function is defined, accepts a WrappedComponent parameter, and returns a component created with defineComponent.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure withAuth accepts a parameter (the component to wrap) and returns a component using defineComponent.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've created a function named withAuth that takes a component as an argument and returns a new component using defineComponent.

steps.title: Define the authentication state using ref
steps.instruction: Inside the withAuth function, create a reactive isAuthenticated state using ref and initialize it to false.
steps.hint: Use Vue's ref function to create a reactive variable. Remember to import ref if you haven't already.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating reactive state with ref
const count = ref(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The withAuth function now has a reactive isAuthenticated state initialized to false.
successCriteria: A reactive isAuthenticated variable is created using ref and set to false inside the withAuth function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using ref to create the reactive state and initializing it to false.
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside the withAuth function, create a reactive variable called isAuthenticated using ref and set its initial value to false.

steps.title: Create a login handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function of the withAuth HOC, create a function named login that sets the isAuthenticated ref to true.
steps.hint: Define a regular JavaScript function inside the setup function. Use the isAuthenticated ref's .value property to update its state.
steps.expectedOutcome: The withAuth HOC now has a login function that can update the authentication state.
successCriteria: A function named login is defined inside the setup function, and it sets isAuthenticated.value to true.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a function named login inside the setup function that sets isAuthenticated.value to true.
steps.feedbackWrong: The login function is missing or incorrect. Remember to create it inside the setup function and update isAuthenticated.value.

steps.title: Create a logout handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function of your withAuth HOC, create a logout handler function that sets isAuthenticated to false.
steps.hint: Define a function named logout that updates the isAuthenticated ref value.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a logout function that can be used to reset the authentication state.
successCriteria: A logout function is defined inside setup that sets isAuthenticated.value to false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your logout function sets isAuthenticated.value to false.
steps.feedbackWrong: The logout function is missing or doesn't properly reset the authentication state.

steps.title: Return the wrapped component with authentication props
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function's return statement, return an object with the isAuthenticated state, login handler, and logout handler as props to be passed to the wrapped component.
steps.hint: The return statement should expose these values so they become available as props in the wrapped component.
steps.expectedOutcome: The setup function now returns an object containing isAuthenticated, login, and logout, making them available as props to the wrapped component.
successCriteria: The return statement in setup includes isAuthenticated, login, and logout as properties of the returned object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning all three values: isAuthenticated, login, and logout from the setup function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The setup function should return an object containing isAuthenticated, login, and logout. Check that you're returning these values from the setup function.

steps.title: Create a simple Dashboard component
steps.instruction: Create a Dashboard component using defineComponent that accepts isAuthenticated, login, and logout as props. The component should return a simple template with a heading.
steps.hint: Use defineComponent to create the component. Define props in the component options and return a template with an <h2> element.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Dashboard component is created with props for isAuthenticated, login, and logout, and returns a template with a heading.
successCriteria: Dashboard component is defined using defineComponent, accepts the three props, and returns a template with an <h2> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the Dashboard component accepts all three props and returns a template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Dashboard component is missing or incomplete. It should accept isAuthenticated, login, and logout as props and return a template.

steps.instruction: In the Dashboard component's template, add conditional rendering to show a welcome message when isAuthenticated is true and a login prompt when false.
steps.hint: Use v-if and v-else directives to conditionally render different content based on the isAuthenticated prop value.

steps.title: Add login and logout buttons with click handlers
steps.instruction: Inside the Dashboard component's template, add a login button with a click handler that calls the login prop, and a logout button with a click handler that calls the logout prop.
steps.hint: Use the @click directive to bind the click event to the login and logout props passed to the Dashboard component.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding click handlers to buttons in Vue
<button @click="handleClick">Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The Dashboard component will have two buttons: one for logging in and one for logging out, each wired to the corresponding handler functions passed as props.
successCriteria: The Dashboard template contains a login button with @click="login" and a logout button with @click="logout".
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added buttons, but make sure each button has the correct click handler: @click="login" for login and @click="logout" for logout.
steps.feedbackWrong: The buttons or their click handlers are missing or incorrect. Add a login button with @click="login" and a logout button with @click="logout" inside the Dashboard template.

steps.title: Wrap Dashboard with withAuth and export
steps.instruction: Wrap the Dashboard component with the withAuth HOC and export the enhanced component as the default export.
steps.hint: Call the withAuth function and pass Dashboard as an argument, then assign the result to a variable or export it directly.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Dashboard component is enhanced with authentication functionality via the withAuth HOC and exported as the default export.
